newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end bourse trade at higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German equities end bourse trade at higher levels.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade strongly ahead on Friday, supported by a strong dollar and firm German bonds and easily shrugging off a slide on Wall Street overnight.
The DAX index ended at 3,298.24 points, up 23.72 points or 0.73 percent in early bourse, off an early high of 3,294.19 points.
"The dollar is supportive, and the debt market is also helping us along," said one Frankfurt trader.
Thursday's post-bourse fall was largely attributed to comments by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan which market players interpreted as pointing to a possible interest rate hike in the U.S. soon.
"Fears about an interest rate hike either here or in the U.S. have mostly been discounted by now," the trader said.
The main feature of bourse trade was Deutsche Telekom AG, which ended up 1.25 marks, 3.39 percent, at 38.10 marks in bourse.
Dealers said that the market was focusing on Telekom as the share, which was floated in November, had been neglected somewhat during the recent record run for DAX blue-chip stocks.
Shares in German steel firm Thyssen AG advanced another four percent on Friday on speculation that the company will indeed be the subject of a hostile bid by rival Krupp AG, dealers said.
Thyssen ended bourse trade up 15.20 marks, or four percent, at 391 marks. The stock hit a new all-time high of 397 marks in pre-bourse trade.
Krupp and Thyssen have entered talks on a possible merger after Krupp temporarily shelved its takeover offer of 435 marks oer share, which it launched earlier this week.
